issue_context.title: better `struct.Struct` repr
issue_context.body:
# Feature or enhancement
Add better `struct.Struct` repr

# Pitch
```py
>>> import struct
>>> struct.Struct('i')
<_struct.Struct at 0x00223FC2C7290>
```
Hmm, what is the format of this struct? It is not clear from repr.

Something like this would be better:
```py
>>> import struct
>>> struct.Struct('i')
Struct('i')
```


<!-- gh-linked-prs -->
### Linked PRs
* gh-107407
<!-- /gh-linked-prs -->

review_comments:
I think this could be updated to the following for clarity
```suggestion
        # s.format calls a (read-only) non-data descriptor provided by struct.Struct,
        # and not the similarly named str.format() method
        self.assertEqual(repr(s), f'Struct({repr(s.format)})')
```

since the `.format()` _**method**_ is frequently used in string formatting as well (e.g. https://peps.python.org/pep-3101/, https://peps.python.org/pep-0498/), and someone skimming the tests (such as me) might mix up the two at first glance and wonder why something like
```
f'Struct({repr(s)})'
# or
f'Struct({s!r})')
```
wasn't used instead.
I don't think that comment is necessary. I would prefer to simply rename `s` to `struct_` or anything else, so that `s` doesn't look like a `str`.

I dont think that comment is necessary too. Word `format` is used a lot in this file, so it is unlikely be confused with `str.format`.

`s` is common name for structs in this test suite. So I think `s` would be more consistent than `struct_`.
